gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-encode-sans-sc: Every stroke of Bruno Ace SC looks ruled out at a single width, with letters spaced far apart. Encode Sans SC settles underneath as a plain sans, with shallow terminal curls and wide gaps.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-fahkwang: Bruno Ace SC traces every stroke at the width of a single stylus, its letters open and spread wide across the line. Fahkwang does the softer work, with faint pressure dips in its round letters.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-figtree: Crisp and stretched out: Bruno Ace SC keeps every opening wide and never thins out into calligraphic strokes. Figtree adds the marker-tip warmth, with a wide gap in its e.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-fustat: Widely spaced letters with open apertures give Bruno Ace SC its stretched, expressive look, while Fustat bends its lines like tubing. Rigid openness against rope-soft curves is what sticks.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-hanken-grotesk: Hanken Grotesk reads like a plain sans bent from wire. Bruno Ace SC supplies the showy, widely spaced headline voice, while Hanken Grotesk keeps wide channels leading into each counter.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-ibm-plex-sans-dev: Bruno Ace SC matches its horizontals to its verticals in weight, giving the headline a ruled, spaced-out look. IBM Plex Sans Devanagari loosens things below with rope-loose curves that never knot.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-imprima: Imprima has a smooth, tube-like look, with terminals that flare outward at every line end. And Bruno Ace SC takes the showier job, spacing its open letters out with a single constant line.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-jura: Jura reads like bent wire, every stroke constant and the s curves opening wide at both ends. Jura handles the quiet text work while Bruno Ace SC does the showing off up top.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-kosugi: No thinning anywhere: Bruno Ace SC keeps its strokes uniform and its letters spread far apart on the line. Kosugi bends its letters like wire where Bruno Ace SC rules straight lines.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-kosugi-maru: Bruno Ace SC spreads its open-aperture letters wide and keeps every stroke free of thinning, setting the display tone. Kosugi Maru does the quieter work, its neon-tube lines glowing steadily.
